messages:
maya: quick Q — we're evaluating Orchid-8B for Dedicated / Private customers. upstream repo has a weird clause about commercial use. can we offer it to paying customers or is that a hard no? :thinking:

samir: link? i can run the license through the scanner.

maya: https://models.example.com/orchid-8b and the license snippet they quoted:```
3. Permitted Use: Non-commercial research and evaluation only.
4. Redistribution: You may not redistribute model weights or derivative weights without express permission.
```

license-scan-bot: Automated scan result: potential NON-COMMERCIAL restriction detected (score 0.92). recommends legal review.

devin: short answer: if that is literal NCU (non-commercial use) then offering the model as part of a paid product would breach the license. we need to parse whether "outputs" are restricted or just the model artifacts. lots of NCU licenses are ambiguous.

devin: also clause 4 is key — "redistribute model weights or derivative weights" — that means we can't ship quantized or compiled weights to customers. hosting in a SaaS can still be a violation if the licensor intended to block commercial exploitation. need to check upstream intent / contact them for commercial license.

elaine: followup: what about Dedicated vs Private? for Private we typically install our runtime + models into customer VPC when customer wants us to manage infra. does that count as redistribution?

devin: if we are the ones transferring model files to the customer's environment (even into their VPC) that's redistribution. if customers bring their own license/model and we only orchestrate runtimes against their artifact (BYOM) that's okay provided they actually own the rights.

samir: and what about quantization/compilation? we often produce optimized .rbin artifacts for lower memory — is that a derivative weight and thus forbidden to ship?

devin: yes, a quantized weight is almost certainly a derivative work under most definitions. shipping it = redistribution. compiling kernels that reference original weights but don't embed them is a gray area; we should assume derivative until counsel says otherwise.

maya: ok makes sense. for hosted API (Hosted Redwood) we would be serving it ourselves to end users who pay us. that's definitely commercial, so blocked unless we get a commercial license.

elaine: product ops note — we need to add a model_catalog flag: `commercial_restrictions` and `redistribution_allowed` so onboarding rejects NCU models for Hosted and Dedicated by default.

samir: agreed. also need to update the quant pipeline: dont generate or store quant artifacts for models flagged non-redistributable.

devin: action items: 1) i'll reach out to upstream for clarification + commercial licensing options; 2) legal to confirm interpretation of "outputs" (some licensors try to restrict outputs too); 3) eng to add hard-blocks in onboarding and quants pipeline until cleared.

maya: thx. can you cc me when you reach out? i'll pause eval perf tests until we have clarity.

devin: cc'ed. initial outreach draft: "We're evaluating Orchid-8B for Redwood Dedicated/Private; your license's Non-Commercial clause appears to prohibit commercial use and redistribution of derivative weights. Can you confirm whether commercial licensing is available and whether outputs are subject to the NCU restriction?"

samir: tiny nit — for Private customers who want us on-prem we can offer an "installer-only" flow where the customer supplies the model tar and we run the installer without storing the weights in our buckets. legal ok with that?

devin: that could work if we never take possession of the model artifacts (no copies, no backups). but operationally it's tricky — need strict controls/auditing. counsel will want that in written agreement.

maya: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:

license-scan-bot: Reminder: please tag model onboarding ticket with `legal-review` to avoid accidental provisioning.

elaine: will do, adding the ticket now and disabling auto-quant for Orchid-8B in the pipeline.

samir: ping me if you want test logs or the initial perf numbers — won't share artifacts.

maya: will do.
